title: CallLint compiler run
description: One execution of the rolling compiler, recorded so a run is REPRODUCIBLE rather than merely finished (calllint.compiler-run.v1; §7.1, §10.2, ADR 0061). `inputManifestDigest` is required and `outputManifestDigest` is nullable, and that asymmetry is the whole point: a run always knows what it was given, but a run that crashed produced no output, and a schema that required both would force a lie (an empty-string or all-zero digest) into the one place a later replay reads to decide whether the run is comparable. Two runs over the same input manifest must produce the same output manifest; the pair is what makes that assertion checkable at all. `state` admits `PARTIAL` as distinct from `SUCCEEDED` because a run that compiled 24 of 25 subjects is not a success, and grading it as one would let a projection ship over an incomplete index. `metrics` is a closed, numeric-only object — no verdict, no score, no free-form prose — so a run report can never become a second, unaudited place where a decision is made. `startedAt`/`completedAt` are injected ISO-8601 inputs, never wall-clock reads (INV-R6, §9.5). Written by R-6; the table and schema land in R-1 with the rest of the canonical DDL.
